metadata.note: The Pittsburgh and Western - Pittsburgh (Allegheny) - Callery - Ellwood City - New Castle Jct - Youngstown - Akron, and its 3 ft gauge Northern lines Callery - Butler - Foxburg - Clarion - Kane - and the Baltimore and Ohio's operation of the same lines from 1 Feb 1902, plus the Knox and Kane Railroad's tourist trains over the ex-P&W Kane line (1987-2004). Drawn from research/branches/pittsburgh_and_western_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), 2026-10-21. Before this layer nothing in data/ drew the P&W main Pittsburgh - Callery - Ellwood City - New Castle Jct in any era, New Castle Jct - Akron before 1923, any Northern narrow-gauge line, or the Knox & Kane. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits: P&W -> B&O at 1 Feb 1902 (BORAIL: 'B&O takes over direct operation'), on identical geometry. B&O stock control from the 1880s and B&O officers from July 1893 are not treated as an operating change (see not_yet_sourced). The Pittsburgh and Western Railroad's reorganisation as the Pittsburg(h) and Western Railway (1887 or 1889) is the same operator and shares one colour; the Pittsburgh, New Castle and Lake Erie (Jan - Aug 1879) is folded into the P&W feature.
metadata.colour_choice: Baltimore and Ohio Railroad reuses the existing B&O colour #00447C, pulled programmatically from data/. Pittsburgh and Western Railroad #9E4A6E and Knox and Kane Railroad #4F6D3A are new colours used by no other company in data/ (checked programmatically).

metadata.reconciliation_4_vs_14: Report block [4] (New Castle Jct - Akron) and block [14] (the Warren route De Forest Jct - Ravenna) describe one main line on two alignments: until c.1905 the trains ran Youngstown - Niles - Warren - Newton Falls - Ravenna, after it on the McDonald - Newton Falls cutoff (FOWLER OH 32). So the P&W main 1887-1901 and the B&O 1902-1905 are each ONE feature on the Warren routing (pw-new-castle-jct-akron-via-warren, bo-pw-new-castle-jct-akron-via-warren), and the B&O 1906-1922 feature is on the cutoff. No separate Warren-route feature duplicates them. The cutoff feature starts 1906, not 1902, because 1902-1905 is the Warren feature's; it stops at 1922 because baltimore_and_ohio_capitol_limited.geojson draws 1923-1971 on the cutoff corridor.

B&O passenger years on Foxburg - Clarion Jct, the Clarion branch, Clarion Jct - Kane and Kane - Mount Jewett: report drawable NONE.
B&O locals on Callery - Butler 1902-1931 and the BR&P's own Buffalo trains over it 1899-1931 (the latter belong to the BR&P layer).
Amtrak 1990-1995 / 1996-2005 on New Castle - Akron: already drawn by bo_pittsburgh_akron_chicago.geojson (with the defects recorded below); not duplicated here.

not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS: pw-foxburg-clarion-jct and pw-clarion-jct-kane end 1894, pw-clarion-branch 1887, bo-pw-butler-foxburg is the single year 1902, and bo-pw-callery-ellwood-city ends 1951 - each is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end. A pre-1951 Official Guide, a B&O public timetable (1910s-1930s) or a 'last train' story in the Butler Eagle / Kane Republican / Clarion Democrat would settle the Northern lines.

Who operated the B&O's Chicago through trains over the P&W 1891-1901 (BORAIL dates B&O direct operation to 1 Feb 1902; the Amtrak layer's note asserts a permanent lease to the B&O on 1 July 1890; PGHB's 1895 source says 'operated by the B&O, nominally under the Pittsburg and Western Railway Company'). A source for an 1890 operating lease would move the main line's P&W -> B&O split to 1890/91.

Start years that rest on construction accounts rather than timetables: Allegheny - Etna 1880 (approx.), Zelienople - Wurtemberg 1880, Parker - Foxburg (drawn from 1881 with the rest of Butler - Foxburg; extension 'begun after 1881', first confirmed 1887).
Standard-gauging of the Northern lines (WPandW 'most converted 1911'; WNS 'the 1920s'; Foxburg bridge 1921) - conflict, and whether passenger trains survived it.
Pittsburgh - Butler B&O LOCALS 1902-1955 (Table 34 exists in Sept 1951; times not recoverable) - not drawn.
Exact date of the Callery - Watters - Ribold to Eidenau - Ribold re-routing (FOWLER: c.1936) and of the Warren-to-cutoff change (FOWLER: 1905/1907).
Location of the P&W's Allegheny station and of Clarion Junction: both placed from OSM grade ends, not from a source; the traced Clarion branch (about 3 mi) is well short of FOWLER's 5.8 mi.
The pre-1905 Ravenna - Akron alignment (FOWLER: Kent B&O station 'op.1905').
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate.

bo_pittsburgh_akron_chicago.geojson | Amtrak: Three Rivers drawn 1995-2005: the Three Rivers ran west of Pittsburgh via Youngstown/Akron only from 10 Nov 1996 (Wikipedia, Three Rivers (train); AKRR), so the start is overstated by about a year. Not edited here.

bo_pittsburgh_akron_chicago.geojson | both Amtrak features: Pittsburgh - New Castle - Akron is three vertices (two straight chords of about 44 and 61 mi) that pass 17 mi from Youngstown, unlabelled in geometry_quality (Rule 2). buffalo_rochester_pittsburgh_railway.geojson | BR&P and B&O Buffalo - Pittsburgh features: drawn Punxsutawney - Freeport - Pittsburgh (Allegheny Valley, PRR), 16.8 mi from Butler; from 10 Oct 1899 to 15 Oct 1955 the trains ran Butler - Callery - Pittsburgh over the P&W (FOWLER 293; WBRP; G52 Table 25 from the B&O station). properties.line: Pittsburgh and Western: New Castle Jct – Akron (via Warren)
properties.speed_source: estimated; not computed from a real timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), routed with opstrace.py: ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (or note:old_railway_operator=P&W, or named 'P&W / New Castle / Northern Subdivision' with no historical tag) costed 1x, B&O-tagged ways of other predecessors (BR&P, B&S ...) 1.6x, untagged rail 1.25x, cycleways 3x, other named operators 12x; waypoints from the research report's via lists, each Nominatim geocode type-checked and bad ones hand-pinned
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap rail geometry (live and abandoned track, rail-trails tagged old_railway_operator=B&O / note:old_railway_operator=P&W) with OpenHistoricalMap for lifted grades: 78.8 mi against the documented about 72 mi on the later route (FOWLER 289/OH 30: New Castle Jct 59.2 - Akron 131.3); no documented mileage for the original Warren routing. Mileage by source: P&W/B&O 69.1 mi, (untagged) 5.7 mi, OHM:(untagged) 4.0 mi, Erie 0.1 mi, (connector) 0.0 mi. Approximated (straight-line) legs: Newton Falls - east end of the old Warren-route grade (0.6 mi, hand-added connector). ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): this is the ORIGINAL Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Toledo route that the main line used until c.1905 - Youngstown - Girard - Niles (De Forest Jct) - Warren - Leavittsburg - Newton Falls - Wayland - Charlestown - Campbellsport - Ravenna (FOWLER OH 32: Burnett's - Ravenna 'Former route until 1905/1907'). West of Newton Falls it follows an abandoned B&O grade in OSM (tagged fixme 'rough alignment in places') south of the cutoff past Wayland and Campbellsport, skirting the south side of Ravenna, to rejoin the present line at Kent; that grade is joined to the line at Newton Falls by a hand-added 0.6 mi STRAIGHT connector (approximated). Report blocks [4] and [14] are reconciled here: [14] is the alignment [4] actually used before the c.1905 McDonald - Newton Falls cutoff, so the pre-1906 main line is ONE feature on this route rather than a main line plus a duplicate Warren route. Kent - Akron follows the present line; whether the pre-1905 trains used exactly this Kent - Cuyahoga Falls - Akron alignment is not established (FOWLER dates Kent (B&O) station 'op.1905'). Between Youngstown and Newton Falls about 9.6 mi runs on OSM track or OHM ways with no historical-operator tag (the Niles - Warren - Leavittsburg line, B&O route 32 later).

segments.note: The Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Toledo (New Castle - Youngstown - Akron, opened 1884, WNCS; AKRR 'P&W reached Akron from Pittsburgh in 1884') was leased to the P&W on 1 Aug 1887 (WNCS), so 1887 is the first year the P&W is the documented operator. 1884-1886 is not drawn: whether the PC&T ran its own trains before the lease is not established. From 1891 (Akron and Chicago Junction opened) B&O Chicago through trains used this line. FOWLER's '1902t' tags on Burnett's, McClintocksburg, Charlestown (1st) and Campbellsport prove passenger trains on the Warren routing. Ends 1901 because the Baltimore and Ohio took over direct operation on 1 Feb 1902 (BORAIL) - the Rule 4 ownership split, not an end of service; the B&O-coloured feature on the same geometry continues it. Headway is an estimate, not sourced from a timetable.

Kent - Akron follows the present line; whether the pre-1905 trains used exactly this Kent - Cuyahoga Falls - Akron alignment is not established (FOWLER dates Kent (B&O) station 'op.1905').
